title: Canonical Rust Validation Self-Hosting and Extended-Surface Parity

preflight.note: Created immediately after WI056 canonical Rust-engine cutover review identified three explicit source-checkout validation gaps: local governance/adopters.json validation remains Python-only, local research/metadata.json validation remains Python-only, and Rust reports a README-checkbox parity discrepancy for completed WI036 that the legacy Python comparator does not report. No WI059 implementation has begun.

acceptance_criteria.text: Reproduce the post-WI056 canonical source-checkout validation result from a clean current main and record the exact structured diagnostics for governance/adopters.json, research/metadata.json, and the WI036 README-checkbox discrepancy before changing semantics.

Produce an executable authority/parity inventory for the current Python and Rust validation paths that distinguishes repository-local validation semantics from retained orchestration: identify exactly which governance/adopters.json and research/metadata.json checks belong in canonical Rust validation and which fleet, research-execution, release, or other workflows remain Python-owned.

Port the repository-local governance/adopters.json validation semantics currently enforced by the Python validator into the canonical Rust validation path with schema-backed typed/structured diagnostics and behavior parity, including all current local manifest invariants required for RepoPact source validation.

Do not absorb cross-repository adopter fleet verification into the canonical validator merely to remove an unsupported diagnostic; fleet_verify.py and equivalent network/repository orchestration remain separately owned unless a new governed decision explicitly migrates them.

Port the repository-local research/metadata.json validation semantics currently implemented by validate_research.py into canonical Rust validation, preserving optionality, configured-path/reference rules, deterministic diagnostics, and the existing research metadata contract without creating a second contradictory parser.

Research execution, benchmark running, external tool invocation, experiment orchestration, and research-result interpretation remain outside WI059; only repository validation semantics required to determine governed source-tree validity migrate.

Remove or narrow the Rust unsupported.semantic-surface diagnostics for governance/adopters.json and research/metadata.json only after their migrated semantics have executable parity coverage; unsupported surfaces still outside canonical Rust authority continue to fail explicitly rather than silently falling back to Python.

Reproduce and classify the WI036 README-checkbox discrepancy against Decision 0014 and both validator implementations before editing completed history. If Rust is misparsing the documented checklist convention, fix Rust and add regression coverage; if the repository artifact is genuinely nonconforming, record and perform the narrowest governed correction while preserving completed-work provenance and history rather than rewriting the past to satisfy an implementation bug.

Add language-neutral or paired executable fixtures/tests for the migrated adopter manifest, research metadata, and README-checkbox edge cases, including valid, invalid, absent/optional where applicable, malformed, path/reference, and representation variants sufficient to prevent future Python/Rust drift.

After parity closure, canonical Rust validation invoked through the public repopact validate compatibility route validates the RepoPact source checkout successfully when no unrelated governed defect is present, without invoking the legacy Python validator or requiring --legacy-python.

Preserve the WI056 fail-closed authority model: missing/incompatible Rust engine and genuinely unsupported or invalid semantics remain explicit failures; WI059 must not reintroduce automatic Python validation fallback, co-canonical authority, or human-CLI text parsing.

Preserve WI050's separate security-critical authority and 8/8 admission corpus; admission, approval, guard, enforcement, IPC, platform backend, protected-service, cryptographic approval, repository-registration authority, and operator-authority semantics are not migrated under WI059 unless an independently governed WI050 change explicitly authorizes it.

Preserve WI057 repository/session/process guarantees while extending validation: one immutable snapshot/generation supplies the new checks, validation introduces no per-record Git/process amplification, and existing constant Git-query/concurrency regressions remain green.

Run and preserve the post-WI056 regression baseline: Python suite, Rust workspace, canonical conformance, explicit legacy comparator, WI050 corpus, linked-worktree/reference parity, frontend/type/build checks where affected, packaging/engine protocol tests, and frozen-surface integrity; no frozen workflow change is implicit in this parity item.

Update authority and developer documentation after implementation so governance/adopters.json local validation and research/metadata.json local validation are no longer inaccurately listed as canonical-Rust gaps, while retained Python fleet/research orchestration and any still-unmigrated surfaces remain stated exactly without claiming an all-Rust product.

Closeout evidence records the initial three-gap reproduction, exact migrated semantics, WI036 discrepancy classification, before/after canonical source-checkout validation, parity/conformance results, process/cache behavior, retained Python boundaries, WI050 non-migration, final main SHA, and any residual unsupported validation surface; WI059 may close only when the canonical validator is self-hosting for RepoPact's own repository-validation contract.

Storage-bounded regression fixture execution: baseline and closeout regression execution for WI059 must exclude ignored/generated build output such as rust/target, never recursively copy .git, avoid multiplying prior fixture/build artifacts, disable Git automatic maintenance in disposable test repositories unless maintenance itself is under test, use task-owned temporary storage, guarantee cleanup across success and failure, leave no task-owned orphan Git/Python child processes, and record enough before/after resource evidence (disk, temp size, process count) to demonstrate bounded behavior.
